source_review.notes: Checked all six references and their cited scope. Fowler's Continuous Integration article is the revised 18 January 2024 treatment and supports the practice definition, daily mainline integration, automated per-integration checks, fast feedback, visibility, hidden work, and immediate repair. Current DORA capability guidance supports regular mainline integration, per-commit build and test feedback, small batches, and repair priority. Verified bibliographic identity, authors, publishers, and publication years for the Duvall, Humble/Farley, Beck/Andres, and Forsgren/Humble/Kim books; they are used for durable historical and practice foundations, not current product behavior. Checked 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined arrival rate, integration latency, work in progress, batch size, pair count, submit time, actionable-result time, and feedback latency before use.
Checked Little's-law, binomial-coefficient, multiplication, subtraction, and timestamp notation and every GitHub math delimiter.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Queue boundaries and stable-flow assumptions are explicit; pair count is explicitly not treated as conflict probability.

evidence: Recomputed L=4 times 5=20, L=4 times 1=4, P(4)=6, P(10)=45, and exercise L=6 times 3=18.
Checked the 35-minute latency decomposition 20+5+10 and the p95 decomposition 30+8+4+6=48.
Executed evaluate-ci-working-agreement under CPython 3.14.4 and matched all seven exact outputs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic examples illustrate bounded queues and timings; no defect-rate or performance forecast is claimed.

evidence: Checked Little's-law application requires stable long-run rates and one consistent boundary.
Derived k choose 2 as k(k-1)/2 for unordered change pairs and checked k=0, 1, 4, and 10 boundaries.
Checked feedback latency separates submission and actionable-result times without implying causality or quality.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter distinguishes queueing identities and exposure counts from causal defect claims.

evidence: Reviewed stale-base merges, large batches, red mainline, uncertain repairs, flaky retries, shared test state, queue saturation, slow security scans, and environment rebuilds.
Reviewed long-running features, disabled flags, mixed schemas, hardware qualification, specialist ownership, metric gaming, and branch-only automation.
Reviewed zero and one change pair counts, non-stable queues, tail latency, later discoveries, and explicit exceptions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Exact commit-stage targets, check selection, and repair thresholds remain system- and risk-specific.

evidence: Traced authoritative mainline, exact admitted revision, per-change checks, visible health, stop-the-line repair, small batches, reliable tests, hidden incomplete behavior, and canonical artifacts through exposition and examples.
Checked that CI service availability, test success, deployability, deployment, and release remain distinct.
Checked repair and revert paths preserve failed evidence rather than rewriting history.
invariant_checking.notes: The working agreement supplies obligations; it does not prove teams follow them or that tests are adequate.

evidence: Reviewed the fresh-base invariant and confirmed branch evidence cannot justify a different admitted merge result without revalidation or established equivalence.
Reviewed health and repair invariants and their dependency on a defined commit-stage contract and explicit exception policy.
Reviewed the small-batch feedback argument and confirmed it supports reduced diagnosis scope, not universal correctness.
proof_review.notes: These are bounded arguments and invariants, not empirical proof that CI always reduces defects.

evidence: Audited uses of proof, invariant, healthy, green, authoritative, stable, reliable, fast, canonical, deployable, and continuous.
Confirmed recommendations, source-backed definitions, conditional mathematics, hypothetical cases, and local model results remain distinct evidence types.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No CI vendor, team, test suite, artifact, deployment, or organizational performance is certified.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet under CPython 3.14.4 with exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit status zero.
Confirmed the model records four integrations, maximum batch two, failure at c3, zero unrelated changes while red, five-minute feedback, successful revert, and no visible unfinished behavior.
Confirmed all team, queue, testing, security, hardware, and management situations are hypothetical teaching scenarios.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No repository merge, build, test suite, CI service, artifact creation, deployment, or human workflow was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed CI as a socio-technical feedback practice: coherent batches, authoritative mainline, exact-result checks, explicit health, end-to-end feedback, repair priority, flake control, isolated environments, incremental hidden work, canonical artifacts, team agreements, and honest measures. Scope is bounded away from detailed branching strategy and deep test design.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed operational failures across stale bases, red mainline, uncertain repairs, slow queues, flaky retry, mutable test state, large features, unsafe flags, downstream rebuilds, slow security scans, specialist bottlenecks, and metric incentives. Controls specify ownership and failure behavior. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified undergraduate progression from precise CI vocabulary through workflow, two bounded quantitative models, four invariants, one executable seven-outcome agreement, alternatives, fifteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked situations, and five exercises progressing from definition through calculation, diagnosis, team design, and safety-relevant transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Sources, queueing identities, bounded arguments, hypothetical scenarios, and one local deterministic execution do not establish test adequacy, defect reduction, artifact safety, team behavior, CI-service reliability, deployability, release authorization, or organizational performance.
